remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Given anonymously [to MOMA]." This and cat. nos. 823, 824, 830 were exchanged in 1936 by O'Keeffe for cat. no. 725. O'Keeffe wrote: "The spring I drove to New Mexico [1934] I went through a part of Colorado where there must have been many buffalo. . . . I got this black necklace there. For the front the eagle claws were graduated in size from a very large one to very small ones where the beans began for the back of the necklace. It is very different from any necklace that one would find in New Mexico" (*Some Memories of Drawings* [1988], unpaginated). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: A banana flower hangs upside down at the center of the composition. Its younger leaves are closed and coiled around the plant's blossoms, while the older leaves have withered and curled in on themselves.
